column1: # Intentional platform-only primitives — exempt from cross-tree parity in validate-skills.sh.
# Drift between the two trees is LEGITIMATE in both directions:
#   - Claude carries legacy/native payloads not yet ported to Codex (the commands below).
#   - Codex carries skills Claude can't run (e.g. image generation) — declare those here too.
#   claude     skills      <skill-dir>          a skill intentionally Claude-only
#   codex      skills      <skill-dir>          a skill intentionally Codex-only (e.g. image-gen)
#   claude     commands    <file>.md            a command intentionally Claude-only
#   codex      commands    <file>.md            a command intentionally Codex-only
#   - Parity: the named primitive is NOT required to have a peer in the other tree.
#   - Frontmatter lint: agents/commands payloads listed here are imported as-is and skip
#     the managed-frontmatter check. SKILL.md frontmatter stays required regardless.
# Graduating a primitive to parity: once a Codex process adds the peer (e.g.
# codex/commands/<name>.md, reworded for Codex), DELETE its line here and the validator
# will start enforcing parity for it normally.
# (dual-blitz, fastlane, run-the-rivers-dry, bootstrap-project-docs graduated to parity — Claude
#  peers now live in claude/skills/; Codex refreshes codex/PARITY.tsv on its side to clear the
# --- Codex-only agents (drift: Claude converted these imports to skills; Codex keeps the agent form) ---
# --- Claude-only skills (intentional unless a Codex feature gap appears) ---
# rolling-campaign chains proof campaigns across FRESH contexts via an external
# headless driver (scripts/chain.sh) — same Claude-only lineage as proof-campaign.
# crossfire-review orchestrates the Codex-plugin reviewer + an Opus subagent from inside
# Claude Code — the harness itself is the dependency, so no Codex port is possible.
# codex-computer-use shells out to the Codex CLI (`codex exec`, gpt-5.5) from inside Claude to
# run computer-use verification — a Codex peer would mean Codex invoking itself, so Claude-only.
# crossfire-blitz routes backlog tasks across Claude models + gpt-5.5 (Codex plugin: codex-rescue
# subagent + adversarial-review runtime) and cross-reviews with a different model — the Codex-plugin
# orchestration from inside Claude Code is the dependency, same Claude-only lineage as crossfire-review.
# ninja-clan runs the whole plan→blitz→review gamut in stealth, routing across Claude models +
# gpt-5.5 via the Codex plugin — same harness dependency, same Claude-only lineage as crossfire-*.
# The Dojo — orchestration-primitive family (see claude/DOJO.md = the rack + forge).
# Each is a self-contained "blade" that slices a problem a different way. Claude forged
# these first; graduate each to parity as its codex/skills/<blade> port lands.
# tsugi is the quiet dojo-voiced pointer (one stone, three lines) — kin of whats-next.
# feint is the read-only counterweight to the rack — every execution blade writes by default,
# so feint walks the whole motion and lands nothing, handing back the would-be cut to preview.
# masamune is the quiet-kin legend blade — one agent on Fable, one cut, total silence.
# silent-strike is the general-purpose quiet blade — one task to a background subagent
# (model-routed, sonnet default), total silence, one line back. Graduate on its Codex port.
# shuriken-storm — ONE uniform op across MANY small disjoint targets, waved parallel volley, no synthesis.
# Converted from imported agents — Claude chose skill over agent (interactive / on-demand / style
# capabilities fit a skill better than an isolated subagent). Codex drift peers noted above.
# Tier-3 reviewers: native /code-review, /simplify, /security-review now do the review act, so
# these keep their encoded standards / whole-codebase scope as skills (the asset) rather than
# duplicating a review engine as an agent. (backend-security-auditor drift peer noted above.)
# Orchestrator pile distilled into the non-sprint coached track (idea -> spec -> build), sized
# below /sprint. Replaces 5 feature/PRD/orchestrator agents. (prd-task-generator drift peer above.)
# Architect-advisor agents -> skills: all 7 were design-from-requirements personas that interview
# the user (an isolated subagent can't), so they fit a skill, not an agent. (5 drift peers above.)
